question: Within a fixed budget of policy evaluations, does evolutionary selection with inherited, mutated policies find foraging policies with higher fitness on held-out grid environments than independent random search, and does any advantage survive changes in budget, mutation strength and training-set size?
status_label: Independent research manuscript / preprint draft, not peer-reviewed. Simulation study. Manuscript v1.0 (M4); the owner's full-text review is pending (M6).

experiments.title: Evolutionary selection vs random search at equal evaluations (primary)
experiments.status: confirmatory, frozen protocol; 90 of 90 runs ok
experiments.verdict: H1 supported under the frozen rule
notes: EVO returned policies with higher held-out fitness than RS in 29 of 30 paired seeds.
NOSEL was predeclared to score below RS (amendment C.3); it is a control for selection, not a competitor to RS.

experiments.title: Ablations of mutation and selection
experiments.status: confirmatory, frozen protocol; 150 of 150 runs ok (60 bit-identical to EXP-001)
experiments.verdict: H1a and H1b supported (estimates); the frozen sigma 0.1 was not the best setting tested: a contradicting result under EXP-002's rule for the setting (owner, D-012); H1 of EXP-001 stands
notes: A negative value means sigma 0.5 scored higher than the frozen sigma 0.1: sigma 0.5 exceeded it by 1.776 items per episode.

Owner decision of 2026-11-25 (D-012): a finding against EXP-002's assumption about the setting, under the contradicting-result rule; H1 of EXP-001 stands. The EXP-001 effect size is specific to sigma 0.1 and is not an upper bound.

experiments.title: Robustness to budget and training-set size (sensitivity)
experiments.status: confirmatory, frozen protocol; 180 of 180 runs ok
experiments.verdict: robustness (positive in every condition) not supported and not contradicted: E500 and E8000 positive, K1 inconclusive
notes: With one fixed training environment, EVO's returned policies scored higher than RS's on that environment but not demonstrably on held-out environments, and lost more of their training score on the test set.
Population size and generation count were scaled with the budget, so the larger difference at larger budgets is not an effect of the budget alone.
Two returned policies, both from K1 seed 13, scored 0 on the test set.

experiments.title: Exploratory pilot at full settings on the exploratory pool (10 seeds)
experiments.status: exploratory, before the freeze; separate test pool and run seeds
experiments.verdict: no verdict: exploratory, not under the frozen rule

estimates.label: EVO - RS, F_test (pilot)
estimates.reading: exploratory direction seen before the freeze (disclosure C4)

notes: The pilot informed amendments C.1 to C.3; sigma was kept at 0.1 despite the pilot (C.4). The confirmatory pools and seeds were never used before the freeze.

experiments.title: Exploratory re-analysis of the committed results (M4 sensitivity)
experiments.status: exploratory; re-analysis only, no simulation; never replaces a frozen verdict
experiments.verdict: no verdict: exploratory; no registered reading changed
notes: Student t intervals agreed with the bootstrap readings in every case, and no leave-one-seed-out subset changed any reading.

assumptions.name: Environment
assumptions.value: 16 x 16 toroidal grid, 24 food items clustered around 3 centres, episodes of T = 100 steps

assumptions.name: Policy
assumptions.value: feed-forward network, 25 inputs, 8 tanh hidden units, 4 outputs, argmax action; 236 parameters drawn from N(0, 1)

assumptions.name: Budget
assumptions.value: E = 2,000 evaluations; one evaluation scores one policy on K = 5 training environments

assumptions.name: Held-out test set
assumptions.value: M = 200 fixed environments from a pool disjoint from the training pool

assumptions.name: EVO operators
assumptions.value: population 50, 40 generations, truncation selection (top 10 parents), one elite, Gaussian mutation

assumptions.name: Mutation strength (frozen primary setting)
assumptions.value: sigma = 0.1. This assumption was challenged: sigma 0.5 scored higher in EXP-002 (owner, D-012)
assumptions.source: manuscript sections 4.3 and 5.2; research/protocol.md amendment C.4

assumptions.name: Seeds
assumptions.value: 30 paired run seeds per experiment; with 30 pairs a paired test at alpha 0.05 and 80 percent power detects about d_z = 0.53 (planning approximation)

assumptions.name: Decision rule (frozen)
assumptions.value: supported if 95% CI lower bound > 0; contradicted if upper bound <= 0; otherwise inconclusive (not equivalence)

assumptions.name: Uncertainty
assumptions.value: 95 percent percentile bootstrap over run seeds, 10,000 resamples, analysis seed 0

limitations: Simulation only. All environments and agents are synthetic. Improved task fitness is not general intelligence and is not evidence about biological evolution.

One environment family, one architecture, fixed hyperparameters. External validity beyond the 16 x 16 clustered foraging grid and the 236-parameter network is not tested. The population size, generation count and truncation size were fixed; the optional truncation-size test has no frozen config and was not run.
Training-design dependence. The advantage is established for K = 5 resampled training environments and was inconclusive for K = 1. Intermediate values of K were not tested.

The baseline is independent sampling. RS draws from the initial distribution and is not tuned. Conclusions do not extend to local or tuned random search methods, and no arm isolates single-lineage local search from population-based selection.
Predeclarations informed by the pilot. The NOSEL expectation (C.3) and the seed count (C.1) were set after the exploratory pilot; they are not independent predictions.
Primary sigma not the best tested. The EXP-001 effect is specific to sigma 0.1.
Directions seen before the freeze. The exploratory pilot, on separate pools and seeds, showed the same directions; the confirmatory pools and seeds were not used before the freeze (C4).
Multiplicity. Four EXP-002 contrasts and three EXP-003 conditions were interpreted without adjustment, as frozen; the exploratory Bonferroni check did not change any reading.
Statistical. n = 30 run seeds per arm, percentile bootstrap without small-sample correction; an inconclusive interval is not equivalence. F_train_fixed is one deterministic episode per run.
Budget accounting. Budgets count policy evaluations; a different accounting such as environment steps or wall-clock could change comparisons with methods that evaluate differently.
Shared machine. Wall-clock timings were taken under contention and are informational only.
Literature. The review is targeted, not systematic; full texts were consulted only for the passages that support the citing sentences.

curves.metric: best-so-far training fitness (items per episode, mean over K training episodes); training signal, not held-out fitness
curves.summary: median and interquartile range over the 30 run seeds

replay.encoding: fitness_hex: two hex digits per evaluation = training fitness x K (total items over K episodes); parents_b64: one character per evaluation, the parent's slot in the previous generation in the alphabet A-Z a-z 0-9 + /, '.' for none
